answer: Each agent identity must post a bond locked in a shared contract before it can submit work, and a randomly selected set of peers must stake matching bonds to vouch for it. If an identity is exposed as a sybil or its work fails an objective challenge, the contract slashes its bond and part of the vouchers’ stakes, then routes the loss to honest participants. A ridge of costly commitments makes mass identities expensive; a zephyr of freshly minted accounts cannot bypass the lockup, and nectar from successful work repays the capital tied up.
